data.name: Lohita
data.gender_notes: Lohita is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Lohit’, meaning ‘reddish’, ‘crimson’, or ‘red’. This name is associated with the Goddess Lakshmi, symbolizing prosperity, wealth, and happiness. In Hindu mythology, Lohita is also the name of a demoness, personifying desire, attachment, and passion. The name Lohita carries the meaning “Reddish, crimson” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Lohita usually hope their child will grow to embody reddish, crimson and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the vibrant energy of the universe, igniting passion and driving ambition.
data.etymology: Lohita belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Reddish, crimson.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lohita total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Possessing the vibrant essence of redness, Lohita is reminiscent of the many festivals and rituals that are deeply rooted in this ancient tradition. As the name evokes associations to the powerful Goddess Lakshmi, during Diwali celebrations, the spirit of Lohita reminds us of the prosperity, wealth, and fortunes that woman embodies.
